Appearance:
 Shri Manoj Malviya - Advocate appearing on behalf of Sh  Malpani - Advocate for appellant.
Shri Pradip Kumar Gupta - Advocate for respondent No.3   Company.

ORDER This Miscellaneous Appeal has been preferred under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the impugned award dated 14/12/2016 passed by Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal,
Neemuch, District Neemuch (M.P.) in MACC No.120/2016, whereby an amount of Rs.9,36,000/-
has been awarded from the date of filing of claim petition i.e. 21/06/2014 to the appellant / injured with interest @ 8% per annum.

Neemuch, District Neemuch (M.P.)

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that this appeal has been preferred for enhancement of compensation amount on the ground that income has not been assessed rightly, which ought to have been assessed on the basis of circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh.

entities.text: Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Future Prospects has also not been NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8839 2 MA-476-2017 awarded, which ought to have been awarded as per the judgment delivered by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs.
Pranay
Sethi &
Ors . reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 .

He further submits that learned Claims Tribunal has also committed an error in not awarding any amount in the heads of Pain and Suffering, Conveyance, Special Diet, Attendant, Loss of Amenities of Life and Loss of Wages,
therefore, pray for awarding the adequate amount in these heads also.
On the aforesaid submissions, learned counsel prays for allowing the appeal by enhancing the award amount.
3. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that evidence led before the learned Claims Tribunal has been rightly appreciated.
The amount awarded by the learned Claims Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.

All the factors have been considered by the learned Claims Tribunal while awarding the Vinod Kumar vs Swarnil Kumar on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79283140/
1 compensation amount and no fault can be found with in the impugned award.
Hence, prays for dismissal of the appeal being devoid of any substance.

4. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.
It is not in dispute that appellant has suffered amputation right leg from knee and also suffered grievous injuries on various parts of the body.

The income of the injured has been assessed by the Claims Tribunal as Rs.4,000/- per month, whereas as per the circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act, the income of the injured on the date of accident i.e. 03/03/2014 NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8839 3 MA-476-2017 comes to Rs.5,520/- per month considering him 'Unskilled Labour', therefore, income of the injured is considered as Rs.5,520/- per month.
6. Looking to the age of the injured 42 years at the time of accident, 25% future prospects is added in the amount of compensation as per para 59.4 of the judgment in the case of Pranay Sethi (Supra) .
7.

Looking to the duration of treatment and the injuries suffered by the appellant, appropriate amount should have been awarded in the heads of Pain and Suffering, Conveyance, Special Diet,
Attendant, Loss of Amenities of Life and Loss of Wages

, therefore, an amount of Rs.50,000/-,
Rs.10,000/-, Rs.10,000/-, Rs.10,000/-, Rs.25,000/- and Rs.16,560 (for three months) respectively is added in compensation amount.

8. Accordingly, the just and proper compensation amount comes as under:
Rs.5,520/- pm + 25% FP x 12 months x Multiplier of 14 Permanent Disability:
= Rs.11,59,200/-
= 50% PD comes to Rs.5,79,600/-

Medical Expenses: Rs.6,00,000/-
 Pain and Suffering: Rs.50,000/-
 Conveyance: Rs.10,000/-
 Special Diet: Rs.10,000/-
 Attendant: Rs.10,000/-
 Loss of Amenities of Life: Rs.25,000/-
 Loss of Wages Rs.16,560/-
 Total: Rs.13,01,160/-
 MACT Awarded: Rs.9,36,000/-
 Enhanced Amount: Rs.3,65,160/-
Thus, the just and proper amount of compensation in the instant case is Rs.13,01,160/- as against the award of the Tribunal of Rs.9,36,000/-.

Accordingly,
the appellant is entitled to an enhanced amount of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:8839 4 MA-476-2017 Rs.3,65,160/- over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.

Other terms and conditions of the impugned award including rate of interest @ 8%
shall remain intact.
The enhanced amount shall also carry interest at the same rate.
